episode_title: 9-6 Every Action Matters with Deanna Benner MSN, APRN, WHNP-BC

real_qa.q: What is the climate paralysis theory that Deanna Benner applies to healthcare sustainability?
real_qa.r: Climate paralysis is the phenomenon where our brains cannot compute climate change when it is framed as a crisis, because unlike past risks that were direct, fast, and short-duration, climate change is not directly visible, is slow-moving, and long-term. Benner discovered this theory while researching why health professionals understood climate change affects health but were not taking action in their care delivery practices.

real_qa.q: How much medical supply waste has Christiana Care diverted from the landfill through Deanna Benner's medical supply donation program?
real_qa.r: Over approximately two and a half years, Christiana Care diverted about $1.5 million worth of supplies from the landfill through the medical supply donation program. Of that amount, approximately $400,000 worth was non-expired supplies that the health system could use for non-taxable status, and close to $800,000 worth of expired supplies came from the operating room alone, demonstrating significant waste from high-cost OR items.
real_qa.requete: Christiana Care medical supply donation $1.5 million

real_qa.q: Why did Christiana Care switch from styrofoam to paper patient cups despite the higher cost?
real_qa.r: Deanna Benner convinced Christiana Care leadership to eliminate styrofoam patient cups and switch to paper cups, which cost three times more, by presenting research on cancer rates, how styrofoam persists in the environment, breaks down into waterways, and affects health. She attributes the success to the credibility nurses hold in healthcare delivery and people's willingness to listen to nursing recommendations.
real_qa.requete: Christiana Care styrofoam patient cups paper

real_qa.q: What three-part strategy did Deanna Benner develop to overcome climate paralysis and drive healthcare sustainability at Christiana Care?
real_qa.r: Benner's three-part strategy consists of: continually educating people about how climate and health are connected and how the health industry contributes to climate change; documenting and demonstrating that individuals and teams can make a difference, and showing that collective impact is significant; and documenting every dollar of sustainability initiatives to gain leadership attention and support for lasting change.

real_qa.q: What recognition did Deanna Benner receive from ANCC Magnet in 2024 and what platform did it provide?
real_qa.r: Deanna Benner was recognized as ANCC's Nurse of the Year for Structural Empowerment for her sustainability work at Christiana Care. She was given the opportunity to present her game plan on stage to over 14,000 nurses in attendance at the ANCC conference, allowing her to share her reproducible sustainability model with a large nursing audience.
real_qa.requete: ANCC Nurse of the Year Structural Empowerment Deanna Benner

guest.titre: Women's Health Nurse Practitioner and Environmental Health and Sustainability Manager
guest.bio_context: Deanna Benner is a women's health nurse practitioner who has worked in healthcare for close to 25 years. She serves as the environmental health and sustainability manager at Christiana Care, the largest health system in Delaware. Her commitment to healthcare sustainability began in 2020 when her daughter experienced severe eco-anxiety, prompting Benner to investigate the healthcare industry's contribution to climate change and develop strategies to engage colleagues and leadership in sustainable practices.

real_quote: I'm just one person. I'm not special. Anybody can do this. Imagine if all 14,000 of us really did this. We really could have an impact that could extend past the walls of the hospital.
